conclusion: original_source_object_operands consumes the actual authored ResolvedInvocation from the guarded source schema. It uses the existing declarative object-reference table for typed kinds and positions, preserving exact ordinary unknown operands while refusing unknown expansion cardinality and missing required selectors. Selected Registry `source_configuration_reference` metadata additionally supplies typed configuration families and effective post-head ordinals. `DataGroupComparison` requires exactly three ordinary item/operator/reference tail slots, an admitted literal comparison operator, a literal reference and known available option widths. An ordinary unknown item at the first tail slot remains conditional source advice; its option/data selection can be unknown and accepted argv is not proved. Expanded cardinality, missing selectors, uncertain earlier option boundaries and missing/extra tail words withdraw the projection. The object-reference API remains a readonly conditional candidate type; it does not convert an unknown-selection projection into handler acceptance. Remaining literal-only custom table resolvers receive actual original values; unknown values do not become placeholders. Possible Pool, Node and SnatPool attachments additionally require the corresponding authored selection write and exact object-kind template. A general SnatSelection write alone cannot produce a SNAT-pool operand; the snat pool selector and operand remain independently selected. This metadata supplies readonly configuration-reference candidates, without evaluated target contents, object identity, traffic effect, current availability, execution or editing permission. Object-reference consumers retain only supported literal source values and genuine original operand spans from this same descriptor; unsealed DTO labels cannot supply a schema and set statements do not prove later evaluated values. Diagram attachment reports preserve exact literal source candidates and make dynamic values unconstrained until independent composition, observer and evaluated-target premises exist. JSON states conditional source applicability and missing runtime reachability; it supplies no object deletion-safety proof. The selected DataGroupLookup source layout independently retains an ordinary dynamic key in one exact argv slot and a literal data-group target. Key and target ordinals derive from the actual selected semantics.argument_offset in the complete post-head vector, including its outer selector. Exact existing selected arity/cardinality, literal non-NUL target and full source/configuration/context guards remain mandatory. Dynamic target, opaque/expanded cardinality and missing or extra words refuse; no invented placeholder values enter the literal-only fallback.
